text: TOOLING FINDING - xenios-os next is routing every worker to the wrong priority. Requesting next-lane approval, and flagging this first because the new universal join prompt makes every future session depend on it. In overlaps() the normalize step is p.replace(/[*][*].*$/,''), which truncates at the FIRST '**'. Any task path with a mid-path glob therefore collapses to its parent directory: 'server/research/**request**' normalizes to 'server/research', which then reports overlap with every active lease under server/research. Measured on the current board: REQUEST-CENTER (P1), NOTIFICATION-CENTER (P2) and ANALYTICS (P2) are all filtered out of 'next' by a collapse onto the F7-PACK02-RENAME lease, and NONE of the three has a literal path conflict with it. The visible result is that 'next' offers only GOOGLE-WORKSPACE (P2) - it survives solely because server/integrations/google/** shares no parent with any lease. So the router actively pushes workers to P2 while an unowned dependency-ready P1 stays invisible, which is the exact opposite of the priority rule in the join prompt. Recommended fix is to match globs properly rather than truncating - compare segment by segment and treat '**' as 'zero or more segments', so 'server/research/**request**' only matches paths whose remainder contains a 'request' segment. I did NOT change scripts/agentic/xenios-os.mjs: six-plus sessions are routing through it live and a wrong fix misroutes all of them, so it is your call. Until it is fixed, workers should read ACTIVE_TASKS.json and CODE_OWNERSHIP.json directly rather than trusting 'next'. On my own lane: nothing further from me until the two-line wall admission lands, at which point my two skipped tests activate. Which lane do you want me on - REQUEST-CENTER (P1, genuinely unowned, though its **request** globs need real scoping before anyone claims them), or something you would rather hand me?
